Bonus Domain.description: When first entering this class and once more at 6th level, the contemplative gains an additional domain. She may pick any domain offered by her deity or alignment, receiving that domain's granted power and the ability to prepare its spells in her domain spell slots.

Divine Body.description: Starting at 5th level, the contemplative gains total immunity to all types of poison.

Divine Health.description: The contemplative is completely immune to every form of disease, including supernatural diseases like mummy rot and lycanthropy.

Divine Soul.description: At 7th level, the contemplative acquires spell resistance equal to her class level plus 15. Any caster attempting to affect her with a spell must succeed on a caster level check (1d20 + caster level) meeting or exceeding this value.

Divine Wholeness.description: From 3rd level onward, the contemplative can mend her own injuries in addition to any other healing she may possess. Each day she can restore a total number of hit points equal to four times her contemplative class level, and she may divide this healing across multiple uses.

Eternal Body.description: Upon reaching 9th level, the contemplative no longer takes ability score penalties from aging and becomes immune to magical aging effects. Any penalties already accrued remain, and she continues to gain age-related bonuses. She still dies of old age when her natural lifespan ends.

Mystic Union.description: At 10th level, the contemplative transforms into a magical being. For all purposes related to spells and magical effects, she is considered an outsider with the native subtype instead of a humanoid. She also gains damage reduction 10/magic.

Slippery Mind.description: At 2nd level, the contemplative develops the ability to resist magical compulsion and control. Whenever she fails a saving throw against an enchantment effect, she may reattempt the saving throw one round later. She receives only this single additional attempt.

Spells per Day/Spells Known.description: A contemplative who previously had spellcasting ability continues to advance in divine magical power as she gains levels in this class. Each time she gains a new contemplative level, she receives additional spells per day (and spells known, where applicable) as though she had also gained a level in whichever divine spellcasting class she belonged to before taking this prestige class. She does not, however, receive any other benefits that class would normally grant (such as improved undead turning or additional uses of class abilities). In practice, her contemplative levels stack with her prior spellcasting class levels for determining spells per day. If she had multiple divine spellcasting classes, the player chooses which class benefits from each contemplative level for purposes of spell progression. If the contemplative had no prior divine spellcasting class, she gains the ability to cast divine spells as a cleric of her patron deity, following the standard cleric spell progression.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: This class does not provide any additional weapon or armor proficiencies.

classFeatures.description: A contemplative who was previously a spellcaster continues to gain access to more powerful divine magic while following the contemplative path. Thus, when a new contemplative level is gained, the character gains new spells per day (and spells known, if applicable) as if she had also gained a level in the spellcasting class she belonged to before she added the prestige class. She does not, however, gain any other benefit a character of that class would have gained (improved chance of controlling or rebuking undead, more frequent remove disease, and so on). This essentially means that she adds the level of contemplative to the level of whatever other spellcasting class the character has, then determines spells per day accordingly. If a character had more than one divine spellcasting class before she became a contemplative, the player must decide which class to assign each level of contemplative for the purpose of determining divine spells per day and spells known. If the contemplative did not previously belong to a divine spellcasting class, she gains the ability to cast divine spells exactly as a cleric of her patron deity. Her spell progression is the same as that of a cleric.
